newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's lower house abolishes capital punishment.
newsitem.headline: Poland's lower house abolishes capital punishment.

text.p: Poland's lower house of parliament on Thursday passed a new penal code bill which abolishes the death penalty and introduces life imprisonment.
The new code, which has yet to clear the Senate and be signed by the president to become law, would replace the current maximum jail term of 25 years with life imprisonment.

The deputies voted to scrap capital punishment even though most Poles, faced with mounting violent crime, want the death penalty maintained. Opinion polls show about 60 percent favour the death penalty and less than 30 percent want it abolished.
But the Justice Ministry argued that the death penalty, abandoned by most European countries, is no deterrent to crime.
Poland last carried out an execution, by hanging, in 1988. A moratorium has since applied.
Since the fall of communism in 1989 just a handful of death sentences have been passed each year for particularly vicious murders.
The new penal code also introduces new categories of crime, including environmental pollution, money laundering and theft of intellectual property such as copyright.
It provides for stiffer jail terms for organised crime and allows the confiscation of property of those convicted of serious economic wrongdoing.
